translation_direction: en → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete English electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Joyce’s flat, exact, ironic narration and free indirect drift into the characters’ own vocabulary are kept without embellishment or explanation.
decisions.rationale: The effect is in the restraint.

decisions.decision: Dublin speech and slurred drunk speech are rendered by register in plain colloquial Vietnamese, with a little deliberate error for slurring.
decisions.rationale: Regional Vietnamese dialects would import the wrong place.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: ‘Faints’ and ‘worms’ are distillery terms (the last runnings and the coil of a still), not fainting fits and earthworms; now glossed as the still’s parts.
‘Twenty after’ means twenty past the hour, not in twenty minutes; corrected.
The remark that the last three words began with the same letter was false in Vietnamese because the B-B-B alliteration was lost; the run is now re-made so that it holds (units 482 and 493).
‘Sure five’ was rendered as ‘năm ăn năm’ (fifty-fifty), inverting the certainty; now ‘chắc như đinh đóng cột’.
Kate and Julia’s address forms were inconsistent; Kate now calls Julia ‘chị Julia’ and herself ‘em’ throughout. The source never says which aunt is older, so this is the translation’s choice.
Cunningham, M’Coy and Power addressed Kernan as ‘ông’ in some lines and ‘anh’ in others; unified as ‘anh’.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.draft_rendering: Hai chị em; Một cuộc chạm mặt; Sau cuộc đua; Bản sao; Đất sét; Ân sủng; Người chết
glossary.rationale: Titles are translated; Araby and Eveline stay.

glossary.draft_rendering: liệt / gnomon / buôn thần bán thánh
glossary.rationale: The Euclid/Catechism trio is kept consistent.

glossary.draft_rendering: dì Kate, dì Julia; Kate calls Julia ‘chị Julia’
glossary.rationale: Gabriel says ‘dì’ to both; the sisters’ own pair is fixed.

glossary.draft_rendering: anh / ông by context; Kernan is ‘anh’ throughout

witness_decision: Selected Project Gutenberg #2814, an electronic transcription of Dubliners by James Joyce (1914). The Gutenberg page does not name the exact printing and the text was not collated with the first edition.

unresolved_questions.explanation: The ‘vermin’ for ‘ermine’ malapropism is rendered by the translator’s own pun.
The Parnell ode in ‘Ivy Day’ is rendered without end-rhyme.
A pun in unit 376 is only partly kept.

title_review.rationale: The collection title is translated as ‘Người Dublin’; no earlier Vietnamese title was checked.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: The opening of ‘The Sisters’: ‘There was no hope for him this time.’
The last unit: the snow ‘upon all the living and the dead’.
